preconditions.description: The number of initial points n is between 1 and 10000 inclusive.
All initial point coordinates are integers within the range [-10^9, 10^9].
The input contains exactly n distinct points.

postconditions.description: The output contains m points where m is between n and 200000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(p in output_points for p in points)
postconditions.description: The output set is a superset of the input points.

postconditions.expression: all(-10**9 <= x <= 10**9 and -10**9 <= y <= 10**9 for x, y in output_points)
postconditions.description: All output points have integer coordinates within the allowed range.

postconditions.expression: all((p1[0] == p2[0]) or (p1[1] == p2[1]) or (any((min(p1[0], p2[0]) <= q[0] <= max(p1[0], p2[0])) and (min(p1[1], p2[1]) <= q[1] <= max(p1[1], p2[1])) and (q != p1) and (q != p2) for q in output_points) for p1, p2 in [(output_points[i], output_points[j]) for i in range(m) for j in range(i + 1, m)])
postconditions.description: The output set is 'good': for every pair of distinct points, they share an x-coordinate, share a y-coordinate, or there exists a third point in the set within their bounding box.
